Tracing the 3s square at rows6-7, cols5-6, then checking upward extension: col5 fills rows 5 and 4 before hitting a 2 at row3, while col6 only fills row5 since row4 already has a 2.

Applying the pattern from the reference example, where the ray span stops as a whole once any column in it hits a blocking cell, means here both columns 5-6 only extend to row5 upward with fill color 3. Similarly checking downward (row8 only), leftward (col4 only), and rightward (col7 only), each blocked one step further by existing 2s, then assembling the output rows 5 through 8 accordingly.
